label: Économie circulaire et efficacité matière dans l'industrie mondiale

sources: IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.11 — Material efficiency, circularity and material substitution in construction combine for ~2 GtCO2eq/yr by 2030
Ellen MacArthur Foundation 2023 — A circular economy could reduce industrial emissions by 9.3 GtCO2eq/yr by 2050
UNEP Global Resources Outlook 2024 — Global material extraction has tripled since 1970; efficiency is essential to respect planetary boundaries
IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.11 — Industry mitigation through material efficiency has high uncertainty due to demand-side drivers

planetary_limits.note: Reduced primary material extraction and waste generation

societal_indicators.note: Recycled steel emits 75% less CO2 than primary steel; reduces import dependence for raw materials
Repair, remanufacturing and recycling sectors are more labour-intensive than primary production

interactions.note: Lower material throughput reduces scale of industrial CCS needed; complementary strategies
Carbon price makes virgin material production more expensive, incentivising secondary materials

methodological_note: Median impact of 2 GtCO2/yr calibrated against IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.11 estimates for material efficiency and circularity. High uncertainty (score 3) reflects complex supply chain dynamics, rebound effects, and dependency on global commodity demand. Resources delta shows significant reduction in minerals demand (-9 Gt/yr) as recycling displaces mining, and biomass reduction (-3.5 Gt/yr) as biosourced materials replace concrete. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5.
